To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the South-North income convergence hypothesis is not supported by theory.

(i) convergence in per capita income between North and South is not a necessary condition of autocatalytic development; (ii) the autocatalytic dynamics of the world economy is not compatible with the process of income convergence; (iii) the process of income divergence between North and South, which is observed in the world economy, is a necessary condition of the autocatalytic growth and development.
“the convergence of per capita income between North and South is a non-event”.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What are the theoretical foundations of the convergence hypothesis? What are the theoretical grounds of divergence between North and South? What is the theoretical explanation of the observed income gap between the North and the South?
the question of how to explain the absence of convergence in per capita income between North and South.
the theoretical explanation of the observed divergence between North and South in per capita GDP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the South-North divergence is the result of a complex interaction of exogenous and endogenous negative feedbacks.
the world economy will never converge to a steady state, neither will its per capita GDP converge between North and South.
the autocatalytic growth hypothesis rejects the convergence hypothesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the South is not catching up with the North. The South is catching up with itself.
the world economic system is not a closed system.
the world economy is not converging, and the North-South gap is not narrowing, because the world economy is in the process of deceleration and stagnation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the autocatalytic model provides a theoretical foundation for the South-North income divergence.
convergence is not a necessary outcome of the competitive process.
the world economy is not a closed system.
